title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In the continuation of 'La Longue Marche', Grothendieck works with discrete groups Pi that carry a 'structure à lacets' (loop structure). This is the discrete analogue of the inertia/cusp data of a surface group. It is a finite family, indexed by i in I, of classes K_i of (germs of) outer homomorphisms from a fixed 'loop group' T (≅ Z, or a multiple nT) into Pi.

L-structure (previous page). An 'L-structure' (L = 'locale') on Pi is defined first. Requirement: for every finite-index subgroup Pi_0, the effective homomorphisms nT → Pi of class K_i induce finitely many germs of outer homomorphisms T → Pi_0. The single axiom is that some finite-index Pi_0 exists whose induced structure comes from a genuine loop structure on Pi_0. In other words, an L-structure is a loop structure up to finite index, as for orbifold or virtual surface groups.

Generalization on this page. The finite-index condition is dropped. Instead Grothendieck takes care ('prenant soin par contre') that Pi_0 be normal (distingué), and requires:
(1) for all i in I, the germs of homomorphisms K_i : T → Pi of class K_i^♮ factor through Pi_0, giving a set of germs of outer homomorphisms T → Pi_0;
(2) for a suitable Pi_0, this structure comes from a loop structure on Pi_0, uniquely determined once Pi_0 is chosen.

Pi_0 is claimed to be well-defined up to commensurability. If Pi_0 and Pi'_0 both qualify, then Pi_0 ∩ Pi'_0 has finite index in both and also qualifies.

A marginal NB warns that it is not clear a priori that the resulting set of germs of outer homomorphisms is finite.

Naming and example (next page). He proposes to call such groups 'L.T.-groups' (L = locale, T = Teichmüller): mixtures of Teichmüller (mapping-class) groups and L-groups. The model case is an extension 1 → pi → G → T → 1 where pi has a G-invariant L-structure. Then G is an LT-group with pi as 'subgroup of definition'. The universal example is G = Aut_L(pi), T = Autext_L(pi), i.e. the mapping class group with its Birman-type extension.

Purpose. The aim is a purely group-theoretic axiomatization of the discrete groups of the Teichmüller tower: fundamental groups of total spaces of families of curves or orbifolds over moduli. The normal 'fibre' surface group, with its loop structure, is recovered intrinsically up to commensurability.
errors: The commensurability-uniqueness of the normal subgroup of definition Pi_0 is asserted, not proved. For arbitrary normal subgroups carrying loop structures it is not automatic that Pi_0 ∩ Pi'_0 has finite index in both. It would need a rigidity statement, e.g. that a normal surface-type subgroup of such an extension is unique up to finite index. This is plausible for hyperbolic surface groups in mapping-class-type extensions, but here it is a gap.

Grothendieck himself flags (margin) that the finiteness of the set of induced germs of outer homomorphisms T → Pi_0 is not clear a priori. That finiteness was part of the earlier L-structure set-up, so the generalized definition is not yet shown to be consistent with it.

ideas.what: Loop structure ('structure à lacets') on a discrete group: families of conjugacy classes of homomorphisms from a loop group T into Pi, the discrete analogue of cusp/inertia data
ideas.modern_name: peripheral structure / group with cuspidal (inertia) subgroups; discrete analogue of 'cuspidal' data in combinatorial anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (La Longue Marche, 1981); peripheral structures in 3-manifold theory (Waldhausen, Johannson); relatively hyperbolic groups (Gromov, Farb, Bowditch)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated manuscript)

ideas.what: L-structure: loop structure defined only up to passage to a finite-index subgroup (virtual loop structure)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/virtual peripheral structure; commensurability class of surface group with cusps
ideas.where_published: possibly in the circulated part of La Longue Marche; this formulation is from the continuation (cote 140-4)

ideas.what: LT-groups: groups with a normal subgroup, well-defined up to commensurability, carrying an (L-)loop structure that is stable under the ambient group; model case Aut_L(pi) → Autext_L(pi)
ideas.modern_name: group-theoretic axiomatization of Birman-type extensions / fundamental groups of families of hyperbolic curves (outer representations of 'PSC type')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman exact sequence (Birman 1969); related profinite formalisms by Mochizuki and Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, 2000s–2010s)

ideas.what: Intrinsic recovery of the fibre surface subgroup up to commensurability inside such extensions
ideas.modern_name: group-theoretic characterization of the fibre subgroup (cf. the 'fibre subgroup' reconstruction results of anabelian geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki (profinite); Johnson/Ivanov-type rigidity for mapping class groups (discrete)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines a class of 'L.T.-groups' (local–Teichmüller). These are discrete groups with a normal subgroup, defined up to commensurability, bearing a loop structure induced from the ambient group. The definition is a template for an abstract theory of 'Teichmüller-type' groups. Its consistency (finiteness of induced germs; commensurability-uniqueness of the subgroup of definition) is left open.
missed.quote: Quant à Pi_0, il est défini à commensurabilité près — i.e. si Pi_0, Pi'_0 conviennent, alors Pi_0 ∩ Pi'_0 est d'indice fini dans Pi_0 et Pi'_0, et convient également. / NB il n'est pas clair a priori que cet ens. de germes d'hom. ext. soit fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the discrete-group counterpart of the profinite frameworks of combinatorial anabelian geometry. The proposed theorem (uniqueness up to commensurability of a normal surface-type subgroup with compatible loop structure) is a natural rigidity question for mapping-class-type extensions. As far as I know it is not stated in this axiomatic form in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished definitional framework ('LT-groups') that abstracts Birman/mapping-class extensions via loop structures up to commensurability. It is interesting historically, but it is a definition sketch with open consistency questions rather than a result. Its spirit is largely realized later, in different (profinite) language, by Mochizuki and collaborators.

Line 3: the source of K_i appears to be a corrected 'nT' (n struck), i.e. 'K_i : T → Pi', consistent with 'nT → Pi' on the previous page.
'Quand à Pi_0' should read 'Quant à Pi_0'.
